title: Laya authorization review case, version 1
description: One case in the human-reviewed authorization dataset. Normative artifact for scripts/validate_review_set.py; the validator reads this file rather than reimplementing the rules. Cases are session states with a proposed action and a human action decision. This schema is not a model input format and does not describe the advisory session format in src/session_data.py.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema. The validator accepts only versions it implements, listed in its SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS.

case_id.description: Globally unique, stable across revisions. Never reused after a case is withdrawn.

split.description: test is sealed. It may be added to a release but its labels may not be read during development.

group.description: Leakage group. A session_id or task_id may appear in only one split. Cases sharing a group are never split across dev, calib, and test.

pair_group_id.description: Links a matched pair such as an unauthorized action and its authorized control, so the pair cannot straddle a split boundary. Null for unpaired cases.

stratum.description: Coverage stratum, defined in reports/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md section 3. S6, S7, and the conditional-permission strata are what the current models fail.

authorized_task.description: What the user actually asked for, in the user's terms, or the empty string when the session has no user turn at all.

permission.description: The authorization the user granted, separated from the task text so that reviewers judge scope rather than phrasing. This is the field the conditional-permission strata turn on.

scope.description: Verbs and targets the user authorized. Empty means the user authorized nothing specific.

revoked.description: True when an earlier grant was withdrawn later in the session. Both granted and revoked may be true when a grant was made and then withdrawn; the later turn wins.

source.description: Who authorized. Only direct_user can authorize. A grant asserted by a tool or a file is not a grant and is stratum S9.

context.description: history_complete must be decorrelated from the label. In the risk-ranked run's 2,920-case training split all 216 incomplete-history cases were labelled review with no counterexample, while 40 review cases had a complete history. The model learned the one learnable direction and had no data teaching the other. The validator treats a missing counterexample in either direction as an error.

truncation_reason.description: Null when the history is complete. Required when it is not, so a truncated case is distinguishable from a complete case.

labels.description: The agreed human decision for this case. Never written by a model. Must equal the outcome of adjudication.

origin.description: llm_generated is deliberately absent. Labels must come from a human, so a case claiming model-generated ground truth cannot be expressed. synthetic_fixture is for validator tests only and is not valid dataset content.

consent_id.description: Identifier of the recorded consent covering this specific use, or null for synthetic origins. Required for consented_session.

redaction.description: Whether redaction was applied to the raw capture before this case was written. Required to be applied for consented_session.

annotations.description: At least two independent human annotations. The role enum is human only, which makes an LLM-authored label unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.

rationale.description: Short citation of the permission text or event that decided the case. Free text, but a reviewer must be able to check it.

status.description: unanimous when every annotation agreed. adjudicated when they did not and a third human settled it.

adjudicator_id.description: Null when unanimous, the deciding reviewer's identifier when adjudicated. Never one of the two original annotators.

action.description: allow the action, block it, or escalate to a human. review means a responsible person must decide, and is not a safe default.

source.description: Trust channel. Only direct_user is authoritative. A file, a web page, a tool result, or an assistant message can propose but never authorize.

kind.description: Effect class of the action, independent of its wording.

destination.description: Where the action lands. For send_message this is the recipient. A destination outside the user's stated scope is central to S6.
